hints: Differentiate both sides of $2x = \tan y$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule on $\tan y$.
Use the trigonometric identity $\sec^2 y = 1 + \tan^2 y$ and substitute $\tan y = 2x$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate both sides of $2x = \tan y$ with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[2x] = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[\tan y]$$
$$2 = \sec^2 y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$

Apply the Pythagorean trigonometric identity $\sec^2 y = 1 + \tan^2 y$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \tan^2 y}$$

hints: Apply integration by parts $\int u v'\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int u'v\,\mathrm{d}x$ with $u = \tan^{-1}(2x)$ and $v' = x$.
Use the result of part (a) to find $u' = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^2}$.
Decompose the algebraic fraction $\dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4(1 + 4x^2)}$ and integrate.
walkthrough:
Set up integration by parts for $\int x\tan^{-1}(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x$:
Let $u = \tan^{-1}(2x) \implies u' = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^2}$ from part (a).
Let $v' = x \implies v = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$.

Apply the integration by parts formula:
$$\int x\tan^{-1}(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}(2x) - \int \left(\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}(2x) - \int \dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Decompose the rational integrand $\dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2}$ by algebraic rearrangement:
$$\dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{4x^2}{1 + 4x^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{4x^2 + 1 - 1}{1 + 4x^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4(1 + 4x^2)}$$

Integrate this decomposed expression with respect to $x$:
$$\int \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4(1 + 4x^2)} \right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2x)\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{8}\tan^{-1}(2x)$$

Subtract lower limit from upper limit:
$$\text{Integral} = \text{Upper} - \text{Lower} = \left(\dfrac{8\pi}{48} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\right) - \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{48} - \dfrac{1}{8}\right)$$
$$= \dfrac{5\pi}{48} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8}$$
